To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) intraverbal training on example identification questions produced rapid, errorful performance; (2) intraverbal performance on example identification extension questions also occurred rapidly, and with a similar error rate; (3) intraverbal extension questions on exemplification and example identification were more difficult to learn than extension questions on example identification; and (4) intraverbal transfer questions on exemplification were more difficult to answer than transfer questions on example identification.

(1) the intraverbal is a complex operant that can be subdivided; (2) the three kinds of intraversal relations used in this study can be ordered in a hierarchy of difficulty, with example identification being the most simple, definition the most complex, and exemplification intermediate; (3) the three kinds intraverbal relations used in this experiment are not all equally effective in establishing new verbal behavior.
(a) intraverbal relations can be subdivided, (b) the subdivisions are related to the kinds of training received, and (c) there are differences between the subdivisions.
